implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy (approved 2026-09-29, effective 2026-10-15, replacing the 2024 version) covers employees, Title and Closing staff, and the about 1,650 contractor agents. Procedures for agent onboarding and offboarding are being rewritten with the Director of Agent Services (due 2026-12-31).

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider vendor; transaction platform vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Employee accounts are created in the identity provider from the HR system and federated to SYS-01, SYS-02, SYS-04, SYS-05, SYS-10, and SYS-11. Contractor agent accounts are created by the IT service desk on a managing broker's request. Gaps: quarterly access reviews run only in SYS-02; departing agents keep access 6 days on average (P07 found 9 of 25 sampled departures disabled more than 2 business days late, the longest 21 days); 3 of 25 sampled employee transfers kept prior roles.
evidence: IdP export; HR feed configuration; agent departure sample (25 of 410); SYS-02 access review Q2 2026

implementation_statement: Employee account lifecycle is automated from the HR system: hire creates, termination disables the same day. Agent accounts are not in the HR feed (see AC-2).

Accounts inactive for 90 days are disabled automatically for employees. Agent accounts are excluded from the inactivity rule because agents work seasonally; 140 agent accounts had no sign-in for more than 90 days at fieldwork.
evidence: IdP inactivity policy; inactive account report 2026-08-20

implementation_statement: Access is enforced by role in each SaaS system and by group in the cloud accounts. SYS-01 uses office-wide visibility, so any agent can open any transaction in their office (about 75 agents per office on average). Transaction-level visibility (own transactions plus assigned coordinators and managers) is planned for 2027-03-31.
evidence: SYS-01 role configuration; SYS-02 role catalog (14 roles)

implementation_statement: Traffic between sites, cloud workloads, and the internet passes the cloud network hub and site firewalls with deny-by-default rules. The headquarters file server and closing-room PCs are on their own network segments.

provider_if_inherited: Banks (dual approval enforced in the treasury platforms)
implementation_statement: Title trust account wires need a preparer and a separate approver in the bank platform, and the approver uses a hardware token. Sales escrow refund wires need only one approver, and property owners can change their payout bank account in the owner portal without a second person (gap 2). Dual control for all three account types and for payout account changes is due 2026-11-30.
evidence: Bank entitlement reports (3 banks); wire release sample (40)

implementation_statement: Users get the least privilege their role needs. P07 found 31 staff with export rights in SYS-02 who do not need them, and 12 standing global administrators across the identity provider and productivity suite. Reduction to named roles is due 2026-12-31.
evidence: SYS-02 role report; IdP administrator export

implementation_statement: Security functions (identity provider policies, SIEM configuration, cloud organization guardrails) are limited to the security team and 2 senior infrastructure engineers.
evidence: IdP role assignments; cloud permission sets

implementation_statement: Administrators use separate privileged accounts in the cloud and identity provider. In the productivity suite and SYS-02, 4 administrators still use their everyday accounts for administration.
Cloud administrator rights are granted just in time through the privileged access service and expire after 4 hours. SaaS administrator roles are standing (see AC-6).
evidence: Privileged access logs; role assignment export

implementation_statement: Privileged actions in the cloud and identity provider are logged and sent to the SIEM.
evidence: SIEM source list; cloud audit log configuration

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks sign-in after 10 failed attempts for 15 minutes and applies smart lockout for password spraying.
Company endpoints lock after 10 minutes idle; closing-room PCs lock after 5 minutes.
SYS-01, SYS-02, and the portal end sessions after 30 minutes idle; the identity provider requires re-authentication every 12 hours, and every 8 hours for wire release staff.

Remote access to SaaS uses SSO with MFA and conditional access. Employees use managed devices; contractor agents use personal devices with a browser-only policy for SYS-01 and SYS-04 that blocks downloads on unmanaged laptops. Gap: the browser-only policy does not yet apply to agents on mobile mail apps.
evidence: Conditional access policies; mobile access report

implementation_statement: Staff Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication with device certificates; guest Wi-Fi at all 23 sites is isolated from internal networks.

Company phones are enrolled in mobile device management. Agent personal phones that read company email get an app protection policy (PIN, no copy to personal apps) only if the agent installs the managed mail app; about 40% have not.
evidence: MDM enrollment report; app protection report

implementation_statement: POL-05 limits contractor agents' personal devices to browser and managed-app access and prohibits saving customer information to personal storage. Agent acknowledgment of POL-05 is 64%.
POL-01 section 4.10 and the training plan define security awareness and role-based training for employees and agents.

Employees complete annual training and quarterly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 6.1%). Contractor agents receive a 20-minute module at onboarding only; 58% of active agents have completed it, and agents are not in phishing simulations.
Insider threat awareness is part of employee training (payee change fraud by insiders, misuse of access). Not yet in agent training.
Training covers BEC, spoofed payoff letters, and changed wire instructions with real examples from the 37 stopped attempts in the last 12 months.

Closers, payoff processors, and escrow accounting staff complete wire fraud training each year. The written callback script is used in Title and Closing but not by escrow accounting for sales escrow refunds or by property management for owner payout changes.
Logging requirements are in POL-03; the logging and monitoring standard (STD-02) is due 2027-01-31.

Identity, email, cloud, firewall, and EDR events are collected. SYS-01, SYS-02, and SYS-10 application audit events (logins, exports, payee and bank account changes) are generated by the vendors but not collected (gap 3).
evidence: SIEM source list; vendor log capability notes

implementation_statement: Collected records contain time, user, source, action, and outcome as produced by each provider.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews alerts 24x7. Inbox forwarding rule and impossible-travel alerts cover all mailboxes. Gaps: no review of payee or bank account changes in SYS-02, SYS-10, or SYS-13; the monthly review of SYS-02 exports is not done.
evidence: MSSP monthly reports; alert rule list

implementation_statement: Alert triage is automated in the SIEM for collected sources; SaaS application logs are not integrated (planned 2027-01-31).
Cloud and identity logs are copied to a write-once log bucket in the shared services account with separate administrator credentials.

SIEM data is kept 1 year and the locked log bucket 3 years. Productivity suite mailbox audit logs use the default 180-day retention, and SYS-02 audit history is kept by the vendor for 1 year; neither meets the 3-year target in STD-02.
Audit generation is on for the identity provider, mailboxes, cloud accounts, firewalls, and EDR. Mailbox auditing for agent mailboxes was enabled only in 2026-05.
POL-01 section 4.11 requires an independent annual assessment and POA&M tracking.
The co-sourced internal audit firm assesses selected controls each year (P07, 2026-08-17 to 2026-09-04).
Assessors are independent of the teams that design and operate the controls and report to the audit committee.

Interconnections with the 3 banks, lenders' payoff portals, the e-signature service, and the mortgage joint venture's lead API are documented in P02 section 8. The joint venture API has a data-sharing agreement; the intercompany services agreement with Title and Closing has no security terms (gap 4).
The POA&M (P07) is reviewed monthly by the COO and quarterly by the audit committee.
Internal authorization equivalent: the COO accepted continued operation of the TMCC on 2026-09-29 with conditions (SSP section 4.2).

Continuous monitoring covers identity, email, cloud posture, EDR, and firewalls. Because SaaS application logs and internal vulnerability scanning are not yet continuous, the company does not rely on the continuous monitoring alternative in 314.4(d)(2) and performs annual penetration testing and vulnerability assessments instead.

Added by tailoring for High integrity. An external firm tests the Closing Communications Portal each year (last 2025-11; 2 Medium findings closed). The 2026 test must also cover the internal network, the identity provider configuration, and a social engineering test of the payee change process; scheduled 2026-11-09.
evidence: 2025 penetration test report; 2026 statement of work

implementation_statement: Configuration and change requirements are in POL-01; the configuration standard (STD-01) is due 2027-03-31.
Gold images exist for laptops and closing-room PCs; cloud virtual machines use hardened images. SaaS tenant baselines (identity provider, productivity suite, SYS-01, SYS-02) are not documented.
Infrastructure changes go through a weekly change board. Closing Communications Portal releases by the contract development firm are approved by email, with no record of security review (gap 10).
evidence: Change tickets; portal release emails (12 releases in 2026)

implementation_statement: Impact analysis is recorded for infrastructure changes. Portal changes and SaaS configuration changes (for example payee approval settings in SYS-02) have no documented security impact analysis.
Organization guardrails block public storage and unencrypted volumes. Benchmark scans of 10 sampled servers found 71% compliance; SaaS security settings are reviewed ad hoc.
Unneeded services are disabled in gold images; legacy email protocols are blocked for all mailboxes since 2026-04.

Company endpoints, servers, cloud resources, and network devices are inventoried. Contractor personal devices (about 3,000) are known only through sign-in records, and the SaaS application inventory is incomplete (P07 found 9 SaaS tools in accounts payable not in the inventory).
Users cannot install software on company endpoints; requests go through the service desk.
Contingency requirements are in POL-03; the contingency and recovery standard (STD-07) is due 2026-12-31.
An IT disaster recovery plan covers the cloud workloads. There is no plan for the loss of SYS-02, SYS-01, or the productivity suite, and the BIA (P05) downtime procedures are new.
Contingency training for closers, escrow accounting, and IT is planned with the first downtime drill on 2027-01-21.
The portal restore is tested yearly (last 2026-03, 3 hours). The data warehouse and integration service restores, and SaaS downtime procedures, have never been tested.
Backups are stored in the backup account in a second region.
SaaS systems rely on vendor alternate processing (SYS-02 vendor RTO 24 hours, which does not meet the BIA). The portal can be redeployed to a second region from code and backups in about 3 hours.

Cloud workloads are backed up daily to the backup account with 35-day write-once retention and separate credentials. Email, files, and SYS-01 data rely only on vendor retention; there is no independent backup (gap 5).
evidence: Backup job reports (30 of 30 days in July 2026)

implementation_statement: Cloud workloads can be rebuilt from code and restored from backups; recovery for SaaS-hosted data depends on vendor restoration, which has not been exercised.
POL-02 and the authenticator standard (STD-06) define identification and authentication requirements.
Every employee and agent has a unique identity in the identity provider; shared accounts are prohibited except 6 closing-room kiosk logins that open only the e-signature service.
All privileged accounts use phishing-resistant security keys.

All 600 employees use MFA (push with number matching; security keys for the 46 wire release staff). About 310 of 1,650 contractor agents (19%) still sign in with a password only after their exception expired on 2026-06-30 (gap 1). Enforcement for all remaining agents is due 2026-11-15; no written approval of an equivalent control will be issued.
Push with number matching, one-time codes, and security keys are replay resistant. Agents without MFA are not covered (see IA-2(2)).
Identifiers are assigned from HR or the agent roster and are never reused.

Passwords need 14 characters and are checked against a banned list. Gaps: 7 service accounts in the integration service use non-expiring secrets stored in configuration files; the portal's database password was last rotated in 2023.
evidence: IdP password policy; service account review

implementation_statement: Buyers and sellers use the Closing Communications Portal with a one-time code sent to the phone number verified at contract. A SIM-swap or a number changed by email can defeat it; a second check for phone number changes is due 2027-01-31.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy (approved 2026-09-29) replaces the 2024 plan.
The security team and MSSP are trained; closers and escrow accounting have had no incident response training on funds recovery.
Tabletop exercises for both P08 runbooks are scheduled: BEC funds recovery 2026-11-18 and ransomware with data theft 2027-02-10. The last test was in 2024.

The MSSP contains endpoint and identity threats 24x7. Funds recovery steps (bank recall, IC3, holds) were not written down before P08; the bank fraud desk numbers in the 2024 plan were out of date for 2 of 3 banks.
Incidents are logged in the service desk tool. Stopped payee change attempts in Title and Closing are logged by the closing team in a spreadsheet, not in the incident log.
evidence: Incident log; fraud attempt spreadsheet (37 entries)

implementation_statement: Reporting duties are in the P08 notification matrix. The FTC notification step (314.4(j)) and the method for counting affected consumers were added in 2026-09 and are not yet exercised.
Incident response assistance comes from the MSSP retainer and the cyber insurer's panel counsel and forensics.
The P08 runbooks (BEC and ransomware) are the written incident response plan under 314.4(h). They are approved but not yet tested.

Vendor remote administration goes through the cloud privileged access service with MFA. The contract development firm has standing access to the portal's deployment pipeline with 3 shared developer credentials.
evidence: Access service logs; pipeline user list

implementation_statement: Paper closing files at headquarters are in a badge-controlled file room; 4 sales offices still keep paper files in unlocked cabinets.

provider_if_inherited: Shredding vendor; IT asset disposal vendor
implementation_statement: Paper is shredded by a vendor with certificates; retired drives are wiped with certificates. There is no retention schedule, so little customer information is ever disposed of (gap 7).
Badge access lists for headquarters and offices are approved by office managers and reviewed quarterly at headquarters.
Headquarters network rooms and the title operations center are badge controlled. At 9 of 22 offices the network closet uses a key only.
This SSP documents the TMCC; reviewed yearly and after major changes.
POL-05 Acceptable Use applies to employees and agents; agent acknowledgment is 64%.
Added by tailoring. POL-01 and this plan make up the written information security program (16 CFR 314.3(a)) for both the parent and Title and Closing.

Added by tailoring. The Security Manager is the Qualified Individual. Title and Closing's board of managers designated the President of Title and Closing to oversee the Qualified Individual on 2026-09-29; the intercompany agreement still lacks the security terms required by 314.4(a)(3).
Added by tailoring. The risk appetite and acceptance authorities are in P01 and POL-01 section 4.4.
Added by tailoring. Testing (P07, penetration tests), training, and monitoring are planned yearly; agent training and SaaS log monitoring lag.
Employees in Title and Closing, escrow accounting, and IT pass background checks before hire. Agents are screened through state licensing.
Employee terminations disable access the same day (25 of 25 sampled). Agent departures are reported by managing brokers, often late (see AC-2).
Transfers trigger a manager review, but 3 of 25 sampled transfers kept access from the prior role.

Employees sign the confidentiality agreement and POL-05. The independent contractor agreement for agents has a confidentiality clause but no security duties (MFA, device rules, incident reporting); a revised agreement is due 2027-01-01.
Contractor agents are external personnel under this control. Their security duties are not yet in their agreement (see PS-6), and departures are not reported promptly.
Sanctions for policy violations are in POL-01 section 4.8; agent violations are handled by the Broker of Record under the agent agreement.
The TMCC is categorized Moderate confidentiality, High integrity, Moderate availability (SSP section 6).
The enterprise risk assessment (P01) was completed 2026-08-07 with NIST SP 800-30 and is written, as 314.4(b)(1) requires.
Supply chain risks (SaaS vendors, contract developer, MSSP) are in P01; vendor tiering is in P09 Part B. 24 of 42 service providers have not been assessed.

External scans quarterly; cloud posture daily. Internal authenticated scanning of company endpoints and servers started 2026-06; P07 found 6 of 40 critical findings older than the 30-day target. 314.4(d)(2)(ii) requires vulnerability assessments at least every six months, which the quarterly external scans meet.
Risk responses are recorded in P01 with owners and dates and approved per POL-01 section 4.4.
Security terms are required in new service provider contracts since 2025; 18 of 42 service providers have them. The contract development firm's contract has no secure development terms (gap 10).
Security engineering principles (least privilege, defense in depth, secure defaults) are applied to the landing zone. The portal design has no documented threat model.
External services are listed in the vendor inventory with data types. SOC 2 reports are obtained at onboarding only; annual reviews start with the P09 program.
The contract developer performs unit tests. There is no automated code or dependency scanning; the yearly penetration test is the only security test of the portal (gap 10).
A secure development standard (OWASP-based requirements, code scanning, dependency scanning, security sign-off) will be added to the developer contract by 2027-01-31.
The portal sits behind the cloud provider's web application firewall and denial-of-service protection.
Boundaries are enforced at site firewalls, the cloud hub firewall, and the web application firewall; no inbound access to workloads except the portal through the WAF.

control_name: Deny by Default: Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Firewall rule sets deny by default and allow by exception.

All SaaS, portal, and site-to-cloud traffic uses TLS 1.2 or higher or IPsec. Email to clients is encrypted only when the sender chooses; wire instructions are never sent by email, but closing documents with Social Security numbers were found in 4 of 30 sampled outbound emails.
Cloud workload keys are company-managed in the key management service with yearly rotation; backup keys are separate.
Approved algorithms only (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2 or higher in transit), per STD-08.

SaaS and cloud data are encrypted at rest by the providers; company laptops use full-disk encryption (30 of 30 sampled). The headquarters file server is encrypted at the volume level, but the scanned 2012 to 2018 closing files are readable by 210 staff; no compensating controls have been approved by the Qualified Individual for agent personal devices that cache attachments.
evidence: Encryption reports; file server permission export

implementation_statement: Endpoints patch automatically; servers patch monthly. 6 of 40 critical findings exceeded the 30-day target (see RA-5).
EDR runs on all company endpoints and servers with 24x7 MSSP response.
The MSSP monitors identity, email, cloud, firewall, and EDR events. Not monitored: SaaS application events (payee and bank account changes, bulk exports) in SYS-01, SYS-02, and SYS-10 (gap 3).
Inbound and outbound traffic at the cloud hub and site firewalls is logged; there is no alerting on large outbound transfers from the file server or data warehouse.
The security team receives CISA and vendor advisories and reviews the known exploited vulnerabilities catalog weekly.
SYS-02 keeps an audit trail of ledger changes, and positive pay checks issued items. Payee and bank account data changes in SYS-02 and SYS-10 are not independently verified or alerted (gap 2 and 3).
evidence: Ledger audit trail sample; positive pay reports

implementation_statement: Inbound email passes the security gateway (spam, malware, impersonation, look-alike domain detection); DMARC is at reject on the main domain.
The portal validates inputs on its forms; a check that wire instructions displayed in the portal match SYS-02 at every view is planned with the next release (2027-01-31).
A retention and disposal schedule (closing files, consumer reports, applications, email) is being drafted; customer information is kept indefinitely today (gap 7). Due 2027-03-31.
Supplier assessments use SOC 2 reports and questionnaires at onboarding; annual reassessment of Tier 1 service providers starts with the P09 program (7 of 11 done).
